## The bug-wave correction train

AgentWorks BOM 1.19.0 carries the correction wave for a defect that made evaluation scores
untrustworthy. It advances Judge to 0.15.2, Journal to 1.9.0, Workflow to 0.12.2, Bench to 0.6.2,
and Experiment to 0.7.2. All other managed coordinates are unchanged from 1.18.0, and the managed
set remains the 72 consumer-facing AgentWorks coordinates.

### If you have collected evaluation scores, read this

Agent Judge 0.15.0 and 0.15.1 could **silently drop a judge from a parallel jury**. The jury still
returned a verdict, still named every configured judge, and did not warn — the aggregate was simply
computed from the judges that survived. A jury rendering prompts on `ForkJoinPool.commonPool()`
workers could fail to load a classpath-backed template, and that judge left the vote without a
trace. It was found independently downstream, where two of six judges turned out never to have run.

**Any score produced through a parallel jury on a BOM before 1.19.0 may have been computed from
fewer judges than it reports.** Treat those scores as suspect and re-run anything you rely on.

Judge 0.15.2 fixes it and ships a regression test that reproduces the defect against 0.15.1.

### The whole graph moves together, not just the judge

Repinning only Agent Judge would have left the defective judge arriving transitively. Workflow's
`JudgeGate` evaluates steps through a jury, and Experiment reaches the judge both directly and
through Workflow. Bench scores benchmark runs through juries. So Workflow 0.12.2, Bench 0.6.2 and
Experiment 0.7.2 were each re-released against Judge 0.15.2, and this BOM pins all of them — the
resolved graph now carries one judge version throughout.

Practical consequence: a `JudgeGate` decision taken on Workflow 0.12.0 or 0.12.1 may have been made
by fewer judges than configured, and benchmark or experiment scores collected on the prior pins are
equally suspect.

### Capture columns that were being discarded

Agent Journal 1.9.0 adds the per-turn cost vector (input, output, thinking, cache-creation,
cache-read), vendor-neutral stop reasons, and tool-call turn ordinals and durations. Every one of
those fields was already being reported by the provider and thrown away at parse time; per-turn
thinking tokens, for instance, arrive one level deeper in the usage block than the rest.

Capture is one-shot per run. A trajectory recorded against Journal 1.8.2 is permanently missing
those columns and cannot be backfilled, so upgrading matters before the next recording run rather
than before the next analysis. The change is additive: no schema key was renamed or removed, and
back-compatible constructors are retained throughout.

### Certification

All five member releases were published through the certified consumer-rooted SBOM procedure —
34 modules, each with its independently resolved consumer closure matching its published SBOM
component-for-component, dependency SCA green, and post-publication proof that the artifacts on
Central are byte-identical to what was certified.
